arguments.issue: Has the claimant experienced persecution or serious harm because of his gypsy origins?
arguments.claim: The claimant and his family have faced multiple attacks, threats, and discrimination due to their gypsy origins.
arguments.quote: Since his childhood, the male claimant has had a life of problems because of his gypsy origins. His children were dismissed by their teacher because they are gypsies. ... some individuals tried to rape his spouse. ... the male claimant was beaten by Croats who told him that he did not have the right to buy bread. ... some Croats told the male claimant that Hitler should have killed all the gypsies. ... his wife was abused and threatened by some individuals ... Now, life is respected. Unfortunately, if the children are taken out of school. ... I have experienced many things in my life, but I do not want my children to experience the same things.
arguments.weak_spot: The other side may argue that some incidents are not proven or are isolated and do not amount to persecution.

arguments.issue: Did the claimant face denial of protection or assistance from local authorities?
arguments.claim: The claimant was refused by police to file complaints after attacks and threats.
arguments.quote: He wanted to file a complaint with the police, but they refused to accept the complaint. ... The male claimant tried to file a complaint, but the police did nothing.
arguments.weak_spot: The other side may argue police refusal was due to procedural reasons or lack of evidence, not discrimination.

arguments.issue: Did the claimant suffer imprisonment due to inability to pay medical bills after an attack?
arguments.claim: After hospitalization for injuries, the claimant was imprisoned for four months because he could not pay a hospital bill of 28,000 kunas.
arguments.quote: After his hospitalization, the male claimant received a hospital bill of 28,000 kunas; however, as he was unable to pay it, he was imprisoned for a period of four months.
arguments.weak_spot: The other side may argue imprisonment was lawful and unrelated to persecution.

arguments.issue: Does the claimant fear for his children's education and future if returned?
arguments.claim: The claimant fears his children will be illiterate and face discrimination if returned, as they are already rejected at school due to nationality.
arguments.quote: If the children are taken out of school. I may be illiterate, but at school we are rejected because of our nationality. ... I do not want them to be illiterate like me because they can no longer go to school.
arguments.weak_spot: The other side may argue the claimant's fears are speculative or not supported by evidence.
